text:
sarah: quick RFC follow-up on a lightweight admit-hint + resumable-trailer flow. main goals: 1) give clients a cheap signal to avoid immediate retries, 2) preserve observability without tracing every request, 3) provide an opt-in resume path for long streams.

alex: sounds useful. two quick asks: exact header shape (so SDKs can parse) and a graceful downgrade path for canaries.

sarah: header proposal (compact, numeric only): `X-Edge-Admit: lvl=2;q=31;b=5` where lvl in [0..3], q=queue-depth snapshot, b=admit-bucket (0-7). SDKs should treat lvl=1 as advisory.

jamie: admit-bucket is good for sampling logic. how do we avoid sampling bias toward long lived streams?

sarah: sample at admit time, record admit-bucket + lvl. long traces only when lvl>=2 or when we emit an `Edge-Resume` trailer. aggregate histograms scrape every 10s for q and admit latency.

mike: streaming resume: trailers are messy for HTTP/2 and websockets. define minimal trailer payload and token rules.

sarah: trailers opt-in via route flag `resume.enabled`. trailer: `Edge-Resume: tok=base64;off=1024;ver=mv1;exp=300`. Token = {mv_digest, wnd, mac} base64url encoded. Size cap 64 bytes. expiry default 5m.

alex: billing and idempotency? if client resumes do we bill from the token boundary?

sarah: billing contract: bill only for additional tokens generated after resume. server persists minimal checkpoint metadata keyed by token mac for TTL (default 5m). clients must supply upstream idempotency key for non-idempotent ops.

jamie: canary & downgrade behavior? we don't want canary instances to emit resume tokens that can't be validated after rollout.

sarah: rule: resume tokens embed model-version and canary-tag. model or canary rollovers trigger token invalidation. for canaries we include `canary=true` in token; tokens from canary are rejected by stable by design.

mike: retry storms: many clients will still retry aggressively on 5xx. can we provide a machine-readable backoff hint?

sarah: yes: when we need to enforce we return 429 + `Retry-After`. include `Edge-Backoff: base=200;mode=exp;jitter=0.2` as a hint. Prefer header-only advisory path first.

alex: perf check on hotpath needed. atomic read + fmt into small buffer should be cheap but bench to confirm. also add global flag for privacy-conscious tenants to disable headers.

sarah: bench plan: microbench dispatch hotpath with header enabled/disabled measuring p50/p99 and CPU. flags: `edge.admit_hints` global, `route.resume.enabled` per-route. dedicated/private clusters default to disabled.

jamie: observability panels I'd add: heatmap of admit-buckets vs p99 latency, resume-success rate, and token-invalidation rate during rollouts. alert on rising resume-invalidations during deploys.

sarah: will add those. action items: I'll open RFC branch with header schema, trailer token spec, sampling rules, feature flags, and canary invalidation rules. alex will take microbench. mike will review token MAC scheme. jamie will draft dashboard tiles.

ops-bot: RFC-1601 branch created: `rfc/admit-hint-resume`. Canary scheduled: edge-canary-4, 03:00 UTC, 10% traffic.

mike: one last nit: define token replay protection for sensitive routes (single-use nonce vs multi-use). default multi-use, opt-in single-use.

sarah: noted. default multi-use with short expiry; `resume.single_use=true` opt-in per-route. will document. :thumbsup:
